Pocket: runs on your processor and starts in about 0.2 s. If the companions use another voice, it loads its own small voice model just for V.

A nearby companion makes one short comment as combat starts and another afterward.

Ten-minute cooldown after a fight. Conversations and story scenes come first. Loading a save resets the cooldown.

Bluetooth audio arrives a little late, so lips and subtitles can run ahead of the voice. This holds them back to match, for every voice.

Auto: 150 ms while Windows plays through Bluetooth, none otherwise. Pick a value if your headset is faster or slower.

The game’s own dialogue has the same delay and does not correct it.

Changes this mod’s menus and notices only.

Character voices and the language you talk in are separate.

Characters sometimes ask about something you said, pick up something from earlier or share a thought that invites an answer.

Now and then, never on every reply, and never while you are leaving, giving an order or fighting.

Cinematic: the game’s regular dialogue subtitles.

Above the speaker: over the companion who is talking.

The Subtitles switch turns both off.

Companions comment after you finish collecting loot from the world. Storage transfers stay silent.

Ordinary comments are ten minutes apart; newly acquired Legendary gear has its own two-minute cooldown.

Pickups made during a fight are folded into one comment at its end.

Companions gesture while they speak longer replies and nod while you talk, with the game’s own animations in their usual stance.

They stop at once when anyone moves or a fight starts.

Companions now and then pause, hesitate, laugh or sigh, as their personality would. Each character decides when; it stays rare.

OmniVoice can voice laughs and sighs; the other voices only add pauses.

Not available with Convai’s cloud voice: choosing it turns this off, and turning this on switches the voice to Pocket.

Each character marks its own feelings as it speaks, so the face changes at that word instead of being guessed from the text. Subtle, set by personality, only where a feeling really shifts.

Not available with Convai’s cloud voice: choosing it turns this off, and turning this on switches the voice to Pocket.

Eyes only: the head stays still and just the eyes move.

Subtle to Strong: the head turns toward you more and more.

For testing and bug reports; leave it off for normal play.

Shows routine popups (joining steps, dismissals, driving instructions, results of companion actions), writes a movement trace in the mod’s runtime folder, logs gesture decisions and adds itself to support reports.

Gang members, NCPD officers, guards, ripperdocs, shopkeepers, bartenders and passers-by answer as their kind of person.

Named characters are not affected.

Gets a conversation ready when you look at, approach or have just talked to a character, so they answer without a wait. Paused in combat and scenes.

How loud the mod’s voices are, for companions, characters and V’s typed lines. 100 is the normal level.

Above 100 the voices get louder, with a limiter so they do not crackle. The game’s own dialogue and sounds do not change.

The next reply uses it after Apply.

Johnny Silverhand answers when you use the talk keys with nobody in front of you, as the voice in V’s head. He knows your jobs and your story so far, and what he thinks of you follows it.

Only while the story has him in V’s head. He stays quiet during scenes, calls, dialogue choices and fights, and when the game gives him a line.

Johnny says something on his own after you meet someone he knows of, finish a job, or a romance moves on. Needs Johnny in your head.

Rare: at most twice an hour. Normal: at most six times an hour, never closer than five minutes.

On the free shared plan each remark uses one of the day’s turns; remarks never take more than a tenth of them.

Off: replies are text only and no voice is generated.

With Subtitles off as well, automatic reactions stay silent.

Pocket: runs on your processor and starts in about 0.2 s. If the companions use another voice, it loads its own small voice model just for V.

Voxtral: made in the cloud with your Mistral key, so nothing loads on your PC. Starts in about a second. English only, and not with Mature content on.

Whichever you pick, a line that is not ready in time is skipped.

Pocket: the lightest, runs on your CPU, starts speaking in about 0.2 s.

OmniVoice: richer, especially on harder voices. Needs a capable GPU and the OmniVoice pack (greyed out until it is installed); the higher tiers start in 1 to 2.5 s.

Voxtral: each companion’s own voice from the cloud, with your own Mistral key, English only. It loads no local voice model.

Convai: its own cloud voice. A voice that cannot run is replaced by a simpler one, with one notice.

Right after the game’s own dialogue with a character, they know its last few lines, including your chosen replies and your phone calls with them.

Only the last few minutes count, and none of it is saved to memory.

A separate multilingual copy of each character is used, so what they remember from these talks stays apart from your English ones. Forgetting a character clears both.

Pocket and Voxtral speak English only, so this switches the voice to OmniVoice · Balanced, or to Convai · Cloud voice without the OmniVoice pack. Without the pack, Natural speech and Expressive emotions turn off.

The game’s own named characters, such as Judy, Jackie, Panam and Rogue, answer when you talk to them where they stand. They use their own voice and memory, and their face follows what they say.

Nothing else about them changes: they do not turn, move, gesture or follow. They do not answer during scenes, quest conversations, fights or rides.
